_about: Tables for body/NUTRITION.md. Rendered by build-body-data.py. Nutrient needs are the US Dietary Reference Intakes (adult men 19 to 50 unless noted); food profiles are per 100 g edible portion, illustrative values read from USDA-type composition data for the nearest modern food and marked by confidence; every food row is a belt data task to verify against FoodData Central before it is tuned. mark: rex | proposed | open.

nutrients.title: The nutrients the body tracks, with needs, reserves and what runs out first
nutrients.source: DRIs: vitamin C 90 mg (men) 75 (women); thiamin 1.2/1.1 mg; niacin 16/14 mg NE; vitamin A 900/700 mcg RAE; iron 8 mg men, 18 women; sodium AI 1500 mg; potassium AI 3400/2600 mg; water 3.7/2.7 L total (US National Academies; NUT-DRI). Body pool and depletion: vitamin C pool about 1500 mg, signs under 300 mg, 4 to 12 weeks (NUT-SCURVY); thiamin stores small, deficiency detectable at about 6 weeks, fatal in as little as 3 (NUT-B1); niacin months (NUT-PELL); vitamin A liver stores 1 to 2 years; iron months; sodium and water days; glycogen about a day.

foods.title: Food profiles for the goods in economy/GOODS.md (per 100 g edible; illustrative)
foods.source: Nearest modern food in USDA-type composition tables (NUT-USDA); period preparation applied where known (biscuit is twice-baked wheat flour and water; salt beef and pork brined months; pease dried; lime juice loses most of its C when boiled or kept in copper). Each row is marked by confidence; all are to be verified against FoodData Central by a belt task before tuning. Vitamin C in preserved meat, biscuit and dried pease is effectively zero: that is the scurvy mechanism (Rex).

ration.title: The Royal Navy ration of 1677 (Pepys' victualling contract), per man per week, with the nutrition it gave
ration.source: Pepys 1677 contract as summarised (NUT-RATION): 1 lb biscuit and 1 gallon beer a day; 8 lb beef a week, or 4 lb beef and 2 lb pork; 2 pints pease; fish days with 2 oz butter and 4 oz Suffolk cheese; a 1697 list adds 3 pints oatmeal. Sources differ on the exact schedule. About 5,000 kcal a day when fully issued (1770s figure, History Hit). Pirate ships ate what they took (Johnson: salmagundi, fresh turtle, wine).
rows: small beer; the biggest calorie source; sours in the tropics so rum and water replaced it
energy and protein ample; vitamin C, A and fibre near zero: scurvy in 6 to 12 weeks without fresh food

body_composition.title: Body composition: how fat and lean mass move
body_composition.source: 7,700 kcal per kg of fat (standard); energy density fat 9, carbohydrate and protein 4, alcohol 7 kcal/g; glycogen about 400 g in muscle and liver, lasts about a day of hard work; in starvation, death near 50 to 60% of starting body mass or when fat is exhausted and protein is the only fuel (NUT-STARVE). Lean mass follows MUSCULAR development.
rows: += balance / 7700 when positive; -= balance / 7700 when negative (after glycogen is gone); floor 3 kg
+= carb intake x 0.8 up to 400 g; -= work (about 60 g per MET-hour over 4 MET); the Endurance pool's glycogenFactor = 0.5 + 0.5 x glycogen/400
the MUSCULAR development sum x a body-size constant; in a deficit over 1,000 kcal/day, development decays (MUSCULAR energy gate)

fullness 0 to 1: a meal adds its mass/600 g; falls 0.15 per hour; hunger (mood push, PSYCHOLOGY) under 0.2; 'could eat a horse' under 0.1
day 1 glycogen gone; days 2 to 7 ketosis, work capacity x0.8; weeks 2 to 6 wasting, x0.5, immune weak; death when fat is gone or mass under 60% of start

depletion.title: Deficiency clocks (the reserve model)
depletion.source: Each nutrient is a pool filled by intake and drained by a daily use; signs begin when the pool crosses its threshold. Vitamin C: pool 1500 mg, use about 3% of the pool a day (so about 40 mg at full, falling), signs under 300 mg: about 42 to 84 days from the last fresh food, matching the historical 6 to 12 weeks (NUT-SCURVY). The other clocks are set to match the medical ranges in the nutrients table.
